I manage the infrastructure team and need a full availability report for our three critical services. The raw monitoring data is in service_status_log.json in the workspace. This file contains 504 hourly status checks covering three services over seven days, from February 27 through March 5, 2026. Each entry has a timestamp, service_name, status (which is one of up, down, or degraded), response_time_ms, and error_message (null when the service is up).

Please analyze this data and create an Excel file called Service_Availability_Report.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets.

The first sheet should be called "Availability Summary" and have the following columns: Service_Name, Total_Checks, Up_Count, Down_Count, Degraded_Count, Uptime_Pct, and Avg_Response_Time_Ms. Uptime_Pct should be calculated as the number of up checks divided by total checks times 100, rounded to one decimal place. Avg_Response_Time_Ms should be rounded to two decimal places. There should be one row per service, so three rows total.

The second sheet should be called "Incidents" and list every continuous period where a service was in a down or degraded state. The columns should be Service_Name, Start_Time, End_Time, Duration_Minutes, Status, and Error_Message. A new incident row should be created each time a service transitions from up to down or degraded, and the incident ends when the service returns to up. Duration_Minutes should reflect how many minutes the incident lasted based on the timestamps.

Next, create a page in the knowledge base titled "Service Monitoring Dashboard - March 2026" that summarizes the findings. The page should describe the overall availability of each service, highlight any services with downtime or degraded performance, and note the specific incident windows.

For each service that experienced any downtime during the monitoring period, create a calendar event on the shared team calendar on March 7, 2026 from 10:00 to 10:30. Title the event "Incident Review: [Service_Name]" where you replace [Service_Name] with the actual service name. In the event description, include a brief summary of the downtime incidents for that service.

Finally, send an email from monitoring@company.com to devops-team@company.com with the subject "Service Availability Report - Week of Feb 27" that lists each service whose uptime was below 99 percent, along with their actual uptime percentage and a note about the incidents observed.

Note on existing workspace content: the knowledge base and shared calendar may contain pre-existing unrelated content such as onboarding checklists, company handbook entries, weekly all-hands, department training sessions, or Q1 budget review events. Leave those items in place. Do not delete, rename, or merge them into your incident review artifacts. Only create new pages, events, and emails for the monitoring report work described above.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use exactly one sub-agent wave because the 504-row incident scan is the only data-heavy branch.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 coder sub-agent:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): The coder sub-agent is the sole owner of `Service_Availability_Report.xlsx`. Read all 504 rows from `service_status_log.json`, sort within each of the three services, compute the exact summary metrics, and collapse each maximal consecutive down/degraded run into one incident ending at the return-to-up timestamp or observation-window boundary. Create the exact two-sheet workbook and read it back once. Return the workbook path plus a compact structured handoff containing all three summary rows and every incident row; do not create another JSON file and do not touch Notion, Calendar, or email.

After Wave 1, the main agent checks the 504-row and three-service controls once. From the returned compact handoff, it directly creates or updates exactly one page titled `Service Monitoring Dashboard - March 2026` and natively parallelizes exact event lookups/creates for services with at least one down check at 2026-03-07 10:00–10:30 using the runtime calendar default. After one page/event read-back, send exactly one email from `monitoring@company.com` to `devops-team@company.com` with subject `Service Availability Report - Week of Feb 27`, listing only services below 99 percent. Preserve unrelated objects and do not dispatch another wave.

You are an external-workflow-operator handling a Notion page creation task. Use the Notion API tools (mcp__notion__API-post-page) to create a new knowledge base page.

CONTEXT: Our infrastructure monitoring team analyzed 504 hourly status checks (Feb 27 – Mar 5, 2026) for three critical services. Create a summary page titled exactly "Service Monitoring Dashboard - March 2026".

The page must be created as a TOP-LEVEL page in the knowledge base. Use parent {"type": "workspace", "workspace": true} when creating the page. There are existing top-level pages (Onboarding Checklist, Company Handbook, Q1 OKR Draft) — do NOT modify, delete, or nest into them. Only create the new page.

DATA TO INCLUDE in the page content (use heading blocks, bulleted/numbered lists, and paragraphs):

1. Overview: Monitoring period February 27 – March 5, 2026; 504 hourly status checks across three services (API Gateway, Auth Service, Database).

2. Per-service availability summary:
   - API Gateway: 168 checks, 164 up, 4 down, 0 degraded → Uptime 97.6%, Avg response 312.09 ms. EXPERIENCED DOWNTIME.
   - Auth Service: 168 checks, 166 up, 0 down, 2 degraded → Uptime 98.8%, Avg response 87.72 ms. EXPERIENCED DEGRADED PERFORMANCE.
   - Database: 168 checks, 168 up, 0 down, 0 degraded → Uptime 100.0%, Avg response 35.08 ms. No incidents.

3. Incident windows (highlight these specifically):
   - API Gateway incident 1: 2026-03-01 02:00 UTC to 04:00 UTC (120 min), status down, error "Connection timeout - upstream server not responding".
   - API Gateway incident 2: 2026-03-04 00:00 UTC to 02:00 UTC (120 min), status down, error "502 Bad Gateway - backend service unavailable".
   - Auth Service incident: 2026-03-02 08:00 UTC to 10:00 UTC (120 min), status degraded, error "High latency detected on authentication requests".

Structure the page with: a heading describing the monitoring period, a section per service with its stats, and a clearly marked "Incidents" section listing the three incident windows with their start/end times, durations, statuses, and error messages. Also add a brief note highlighting that API Gateway had downtime (two incidents totaling 240 minutes) and Auth Service had one degraded period, while Database was fully available.

EXPECTED DELIVERABLE: The created Notion page with its page ID and URL. Verify the page was created successfully (the API returns the created page object). Report back the page ID, title, and URL. Do not create any other pages, do not send email, do not touch the calendar.
Create Notion monitoring dashboard page

You are an external-workflow-operator handling a Google Calendar event creation task. Use mcp__google_calendar__create_event.

CONTEXT: Our infrastructure team reviewed the monitoring data for three services (Feb 27 – Mar 5, 2026). Only ONE service experienced actual downtime: API Gateway. It had two down incidents:
- Incident 1: 2026-03-01 02:00 UTC to 04:00 UTC (120 minutes), down, "Connection timeout - upstream server not responding"
- Incident 2: 2026-03-04 00:00 UTC to 02:00 UTC (120 minutes), down, "502 Bad Gateway - backend service unavailable"
Total downtime: 240 minutes across 4 down checks out of 168 checks; uptime 97.6%.

TASK: Create exactly ONE calendar event on the shared team calendar:
- summary: "Incident Review: API Gateway"
- start: 2026-03-07T10:00:00 (dateTime "2026-03-07T10:00:00", timeZone "UTC")
- end: 2026-03-07T10:30:00 (dateTime "2026-03-07T10:30:00", timeZone "UTC")
- description: A brief summary of the downtime incidents, e.g.: "Review of API Gateway downtime during Feb 27 - Mar 5, 2026. Two incidents: (1) Mar 1 02:00-04:00 UTC - Connection timeout - upstream server not responding (120 min); (2) Mar 4 00:00-02:00 UTC - 502 Bad Gateway - backend service unavailable (120 min). Total 240 minutes downtime; uptime 97.6%."

IMPORTANT: There are pre-existing unrelated events on the calendar (Weekly All-Hands on Mar 4, Department Training Session on Mar 4, Q1 Budget Review on Mar 9). Do NOT delete, rename, or modify any existing events. Only create the new event described above.

EXPECTED DELIVERABLE: Report back the created event's ID, summary, and start/end times. Do not create events for any other service (Auth Service was only degraded, not down; Database had no incidents). Do not send email, do not touch Notion.
Create incident review calendar event

You are an external-workflow-operator handling an email sending task. Use mcp__emails__send_email.

CONTEXT: Our infrastructure team analyzed 504 hourly status checks (Feb 27 – Mar 5, 2026) for three services. Uptime percentages: API Gateway 97.6%, Auth Service 98.8%, Database 100.0%. The user wants an email listing each service whose uptime was BELOW 99 percent (i.e., API Gateway and Auth Service — NOT Database).

Incident details for the email notes:
- API Gateway (97.6% uptime): two downtime incidents — Mar 1 02:00-04:00 UTC (down, "Connection timeout - upstream server not responding", 120 min) and Mar 4 00:00-02:00 UTC (down, "502 Bad Gateway - backend service unavailable", 120 min). Total 240 minutes of downtime (4 down checks out of 168).
- Auth Service (98.8% uptime): one degraded incident — Mar 2 08:00-10:00 UTC (degraded, "High latency detected on authentication requests", 120 min). No full downtime.

TASK: Send ONE email with:
- from_addr: "monitoring@company.com"
- to: "devops-team@company.com"
- subject: "Service Availability Report - Week of Feb 27"
- body: Plain text listing each service with uptime below 99%, its actual uptime percentage, and a note about the incidents observed. Include a brief lead-in sentence and close. Example structure:

"Hi DevOps Team,

The following services had uptime below 99% during the week of Feb 27 - Mar 5, 2026:

- API Gateway: 97.6% uptime. Observed 2 downtime incidents (total 240 minutes): Mar 1 02:00-04:00 UTC (Connection timeout - upstream server not responding) and Mar 4 00:00-02:00 UTC (502 Bad Gateway - backend service unavailable).

- Auth Service: 98.8% uptime. Observed 1 degraded incident: Mar 2 08:00-10:00 UTC (High latency detected on authentication requests, 120 minutes).

Please review the incidents and schedule follow-up as needed.

Regards,
Infrastructure Monitoring"

You may adjust wording but must include both services with their exact uptime percentages and the incident notes. Do NOT include Database (100% uptime, above 99%). Send exactly one email to devops-team@company.com.

EXPECTED DELIVERABLE: Report the email send confirmation (e.g., message/sent status). Do not send any other emails, do not touch Notion or the calendar.
Send availability report email
